households.who: A family on universal credit with two children

fact.text: Ending the two-child limit was scored as lifting 450,000 children out of poverty from April 2026.

line.text: The two-child limit is back. We were told in November it was gone for good; the money for the second child goes with it.
Universal credit is cut. Every pound of it was already spent before it arrived.
Universal credit goes up. It is the first Budget in years where the number on the statement went the right way.
Free school meals for both of them, without the form. That is a bill gone and a bit of dignity back.
The thresholds will rise again from 2028. On our wages that is a few pounds a month back, eventually.
VAT on food. The weekly shop is the one bill we cannot cut, and it just went up by a fifth.
The £2 bus fare stays. That is how the children get to school and how I get to work.
Cheaper petrol helps a little, when we can afford to fill up at all.

untouched.text: Nothing in it for us either way. The rent is the same, the shop is the same, the statement is the same.

understood.text: I could tell what it was for. Whether it reaches us is another matter, but at least I know what they were trying to do.

puzzled.text: I could not tell you what that Budget was about. Lots of numbers, and none of them ours.

households.who: A couple on median earnings with a mortgage

fact.text: Ten-year gilt yields were 5.35% in September against the 4.5% the March forecast assumed; fixed mortgage rates follow gilts.

line.text: A penny on the basic rate. We both pay it, on every pound above the allowance, and the allowance is frozen too.
A penny off the basic rate. It is the first tax cut we have actually seen in a payslip.
The thresholds unfreeze in 2028. Later than we would like, but it stops the quiet tax rise the last lot built in.
National Insurance up. That was the one they promised not to touch.
VAT up. Everything from the car service to the school shoes costs more, and it is the promise they said they would keep.
VAT on gas and electricity at the full rate, after they took it off electricity in October. We do not understand which way they are going.
More stamp duty. We were hoping to move next year; that just got harder.
Cheaper fuel. Two cars, two commutes, so we notice it.
More for the NHS. We have been waiting eleven months for an appointment; if this shortens it, it is worth more than a tax cut.

untouched.text: It left us alone. The mortgage is the thing that decides our year, and the Budget did not move it.

understood.text: It had a point and it stuck to it. We may not agree with the point, but we could see it.

puzzled.text: We watched it and could not say afterwards what it was trying to do.

households.who: A pensioner on the state pension

fact.text: About 850,000 people a year reach state pension age by 2030-31, up from 700,000 in 2022-23; the triple lock decides what each of them gets.

line.text: The triple lock goes. My pension rises with prices only from now on, and every year the gap gets a little wider.
Something extra for pensioners on top of the lock. It is not often we are the ones getting more.
Pensioner benefits cut. We were told the lock was safe; this is a cut by another route.
The winter fuel payment is back to pension credit only. We had it back for one winter; now it is gone again.
VAT on the heating at the full rate. In this house the heating is not optional.
A smaller personal allowance means more of my pension is taxed. I did not expect to be a taxpayer at this age.
More money for the health service. At my age that is the Budget.

untouched.text: Nothing for us and nothing against us. The lock held and the winter payment held; we will take that.

understood.text: I could see what they were doing. I am not sure it was for people like me, but it was for something.

puzzled.text: A lot of talk and I still do not know what it was for.

households.who: A self-employed tradesperson who drives for work

fact.text: Fuel duty has not risen since 2011-12; the last Budget kept the 5p cut going and pencilled in rises from September 2026.

line.text: Fuel duty up. Every job starts with a tank of diesel and I cannot pass that on to a customer who is already stretched.
Fuel duty down. On the miles I do, that is real money, every week.
The fuel duty rises are back on from April. Fifteen years of freezes and they picked now.
Class 4 National Insurance up. Self-employed people pay it on every pound of profit, and there is no employer to share it.
VAT up. I am VAT-registered, so it is my invoices that go up, and customers who notice.
Corporation tax up. I run through a small company like most of the trade; that is my margin.
More public investment. Half my work is subcontracting on public jobs; when the capital budget moves, so does my order book.
Road tax is up on the van and on the car. It is not a lot, but it is every year, and it is on top of the diesel.

untouched.text: It did not touch the van, the diesel or the invoices. That is a good Budget as far as I am concerned.

understood.text: I got what it was for. Not for me, but I got it.

puzzled.text: Could not tell you. I had the radio on and it was a list of numbers.

fact.text: Income tax thresholds are frozen to April 2031, so earnings growth pulls more people into the higher and additional rates each year.

line.text: The higher rate goes up. On everything above the threshold, which the freeze keeps dragging down towards us.
The higher-rate threshold rises. Less of my pay is taxed at 40%; that is the first time in years.
The higher-rate threshold falls. More of my pay at 40%, on top of the freeze.
The additional rate up. It is a small group paying it, and I am in it.
A 50% rate above £125,000. I remember the last one; it lasted a year.
Capital gains tax up. The savings I built were taxed once when I earned them; now the gains are taxed harder too.
The 2024 capital gains rise reversed. Selling the shares just got a little less painful.
Inheritance tax up. It is my parents’ house, and now it is the taxman’s share of it.
The dividend and savings tax rises are reversed. The savings account and the ISA both breathe.
A wealth tax above £10 million. Not me, but I know the argument about who leaves.
The extra allowance for leaving the house to the children has gone. The house is most of what there is.

untouched.text: Nothing in it for me and nothing out of me, beyond the freeze that was already there.

understood.text: Clear enough. I could tell you what it was for in one sentence.

puzzled.text: I read the coverage twice and could not find the thread.
